1. Introduction to Linear Regression 
Linear  Regression  is  a  foundational  algorithm  in  machine  learning  and  statistics  used  for 
predicting  continuous  numerical  values.  It  establishes  a  mathematical  relationship  between 
input variables (features) and an output variable (target) using a linear function. 
Linear Regression is widely applied due to its simplicity, interpretability, and efficiency, and it 
forms the basis for more advanced regression techniques. 
Types of Linear Regression

We cannot randomly create many best-fit lines and check which one minimizes the error, as this 
is inefficient. Instead, we use an optimization technique where we start with one best fit line and 
iteratively  adjust  the  values  of θ0 and θ1 to  minimize  the total  error.  This  process  involves 
"rotating" the line by changing these parameters to find the optimal fit.

This curve represents the gradient descent. Gradient descent is a crucial concept used to find the 
minimum of the cost function by iteratively updating the parameters θ0 and θ1. 
Our goal is to reach the global minimum point on this curve, which corresponds to the best-fit line 
with minimal error. This is achieved by adjusting θ0 and θ1 values accordingly. 
Since we assumed θ0=0 (line passing through the origin), we only varied θ1. However, in general, 
both parameters are adjusted to minimize the cost function. 
Randomly selecting different θ1 values is not efficient. Instead, we need a convergence algorithm 
that systematically updates θ1 (and θ0) to find the minimum of the cost function.

Equation of the Best-Fit Line 
For simple linear regression (with one independent variable), the best-fit line is represented by 
the equation 
y=mx+b 
Where: 
y is the predicted value (dependent variable) 
x is the input (independent variable) 
m is the slope of the line (how much y changes when x changes) 
b is the intercept (the value of y when x = 0) 
The best-fit line will be the one that optimizes the values of m (slope) and b (intercept) so that 
the predicted y values are as close as possible to the actual data points. 
Finding the Best Fit Line 
We  discussed  above  that  different  set  of  parameters  will  provide  different  regression  lines. 
However, each regression line does not represent the optimal relation between the input and output 
values. The main goal is to find the best-fit line. 
A  regression  line  is  said to  be  the  best  fit  if  the  error  between  actual  and  predicted  values  is 
minimal.
